title: Same, tie or different

blocks.text: A hospital schedules its operating theatres with a MILP every night, and the job is now run twice to check it. Each run gives a dict: `status` (a string such as `"OPTIMAL"` or `"FEASIBLE"`), `objective` (a float) and `plan`, a dict from each surgery's id to its theatre, for example `{"S1": "T2", "S2": "T1"}`.
Write `verdict(first, second, tol)` that returns one word for the pair:

items: `"same"`: the two runs stopped for the same reason, their objectives are within `tol` of each other, and they made the same assignments;
`"tie"`: the same status and objectives within `tol`, but different assignments: an equally good other plan;

blocks.text:
"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from verdict import verdict

run = {"status": "OPTIMAL", "objective": 64.0, "plan": {"K1": "R3", "K2": "R1", "K3": "R2"}}

print("same run again:", verdict(run, dict(run)))
print("K1 and K2 swap rooms:", verdict(run, {**run, "plan": {"K1": "R1", "K2": "R3", "K3": "R2"}}))
print("objective 64.0000000002:", verdict(run, {**run, "objective": 64.0000000002}))
print("objective 61:", verdict(run, {**run, "objective": 61.0}))
print("status FEASIBLE:", verdict(run, {**run, "status": "FEASIBLE"}))

cases.says: two identical runs are the same, an equally good other plan is a tie, and a run worth less is different
objectives that differ by less than the tolerance count as equal
the same assignments listed in another order are the same plan
a FEASIBLE run and an OPTIMAL run with the same plan and value are different

origin.section: When Plans Tie, Input Order Picks the Winner

concepts: a rerun is the same, a tie or a different result, and status, value and plan each decide
